messages.subject: Rmatrix2mvOneVar not found
parts:
Hi

I'm working through the script called "aboutNimbleSupplement.R" posted as online suplementary matrial to the paper "Programming with models:..."

http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10618600.2016.1172487. 

For the importance sampler example, when I try running the following lines 

## put sample matrix into ISsample modelValues object
Rmatrix2mvOneVar(sample, ISsample, 'theta', 1000L)

I get the error

Error: could not find function "Rmatrix2mvOneVar"

I had been using a development version of nimble downloaded from github on the 11th July. I just updated to todays devel version - same result.

I see in the html help that there is / was a "matrix2mv" function too, typing that into the R terminal also returns a not found error message.

Are Rmatrix2mvOneVar and matrix2mv now obsolete? If so what should I be using instead?

messages.subject: Re: Rmatrix2mvOneVar not found
parts:
Thanks Perry

I have been trying to make my own nimble function 'matrix2modelValues' to copy matrix elements to a modelValues object and have hit  a brick wall with a compilation error.

Here's the function. The nimble version appears to work fine, it is compilation that bugs.

matrix2modelValues <- nimbleFunction(
    setup = function (model, ModelValues, targetNode) { } ,
    run= function (aMatrix, indexVector) {
        nrMatrix <- nrow(aMatrix)
        if (nrMatrix != getsize(ModelValues))
            resize(ModelValues, nrMatrix)
        for (ii in 1:nrMatrix) {
            for (jj in 1:length(indexVector)) {
                ## browser() 
                ModelValues[targetNode,ii][indexVector[jj]] <<- aMatrix[ii,indexVector[jj]] 
            }
        }
    } 
)

Here's the compilation error

matrix2ISsample     <- matrix2modelValues(model=pumpModel, ModelValues=ISsample, targetNode='theta')   ## This function works fine in Nimble
cMatrix2ISsample2 <- compileNimble(matrix2ISsample) 
Error in AT$default : object of type 'symbol' is not subsettable

I've tried numerous different flavours of this function, but this particular error message is quite tenacious. The full script is attached for reproducibility.

Curiously,  if I uncomment the "## browser()" line and type model when the nimble function stops there I get "Error: object 'model' not found" - surely everything declared in setup should be visible in the run code no?

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Rmatrix2mvOneVar not found
parts:
David, that's a valiant go at writing that nimbleFunction!  Just a few things were getting you down:

(1) The particularly tenacious compilation error you were getting is something we really need to add a better error message for.  That's for when you forget to put the type declarations for run-time arguments, e.g.
run = function( aMatrix = double(2), ...)

(2) NIMBLE DSL doesn't support nrow(matrix).  Instead, use dim(matrix)[1]

(3) NIMBLE DSL doesn't support length(vector).  Instead, use dim(vector)[1]

Those changes are made in the attached script, which compiles, runs, and gives results as you would expect.

Keep at it!
Daniel

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Rmatrix2mvOneVar not found
parts: I just realized I neglected to answer your other question -- which is a good one.
>> surely everything declared in setup should be visible in the run code no?

No, not automatically.  nimbleFunctions are written to be clever enough to *inspect* the run function code (and also any other member methods, if any exist), and see what variables are used.  Then *only preserve* the setup function declarations (both setup function arguments, and variables declared in the body of the setup function) which appear somewhere in the run function (or in a member method).

So, since "model" doesn't appear anywhere in the run function, it isn't available later on.

You can *force* any particular setup declarations to be available, regardless if they're used or not, but adding this line anywhere in the body of the setup function:

setupOutputs(var1, var2, var3, .....), or in your case:

setupOutputs(model)

I know that's covered somewhere in the manual, it looks like section 9.4.1 "Control of setup outputs".

Cheers,
Daniel
